product_boundary: exactly one executable file named EntityOS

observed_anchors.clayvm_bytes: CLAYVM/2 already admits owned immutable Bytes for function parameters/returns and rejects mutable or borrowed byte exporters without an epoch/lease contract.
observed_anchors.hostcall_gap: OP_HOSTCALL still rejects every non-int argument and ClayHost is still list[int] -> int, while exact hostcall signatures currently live only in executable_ir_adapter.py.
observed_anchors.existing_real_bytes_source: HostProcessReceipt already records bounded stdout and stderr as built-in immutable bytes after direct shell=false Linux process execution.
observed_anchors.existing_request_identity: HostProcessVMHost already maps an admitted Int request_id to a completed HostProcessReceipt and fails closed for unknown receipt IDs.

architecture_decision.mechanism: one versioned canonical hostcall ABI registry keyed by stable call_id and imported by both executable lowering and ClayVM runtime
architecture_decision.runtime_rule: ClayVM validates both hostcall arguments and the host return value against the same immutable ABI contract used by lowering; host adapters do not define Clay type semantics.
architecture_decision.rejected_shortcut: generic ClayValue widening without VM-enforced per-call signature authority

first_real_bytes_contract.candidate_call_semantics: Given an already-admitted completed process request_id, return the exact bounded HostProcessReceipt.stdout bytes without text decoding, transcoding, parsing or hidden shell semantics.
first_real_bytes_contract.ownership: HostProcessReceipt.stdout is already a built-in immutable bytes snapshot produced by the bounded process capture path; ClayVM Bytes admission must preserve exact octets.
first_real_bytes_contract.payload_semantics: opaque bytes; NUL and non-UTF-8 octets are data and must not be interpreted as text
first_real_bytes_contract.bound: inherits the existing admitted process capture max_output_bytes bound for the originating request
first_real_bytes_contract.why_real_not_test_echo: Clay-visible byte-preserving stdout is an explicit CM-TERM requirement and already exists as a canonical process receipt payload; this exercises required product behavior rather than inventing test-only echo semantics.

scope_and_nonclaims.proves_when_implemented_and_tested: first real Bytes return crossing from the host capability boundary through the single ClayVM into a Clay-visible value
does_not_prove: Bytes arguments from Clay to host
whole EntityOS or Clay Computer PASS
scope_and_nonclaims.request_id_limit: The existing Int request_id is retained only for this bounded already-present process bridge. It must not be generalized into a hidden untyped byte-buffer handle architecture; future first-class Process/Buffer resource semantics remain open.

counterhypotheses_and_required_falsifier.counterhypothesis: The shared registry becomes a second semantic authority that can disagree with TypedIR.
counterhypotheses_and_required_falsifier.falsifier: A TypedIR capability/signature/type disagreement with the registry must fail before VM execution; no adapter override is accepted.

counterhypotheses_and_required_falsifier.counterhypothesis: The VM still trusts a host adapter return value.
counterhypotheses_and_required_falsifier.falsifier: Force the Int->Int legacy hostcall to return Bytes and force the stdout Int->Bytes hostcall to return Int; both must trap at the VM hostcall boundary before the value reaches a Clay caller frame.

counterhypotheses_and_required_falsifier.counterhypothesis: Opaque stdout bytes are accidentally treated as text.
counterhypotheses_and_required_falsifier.falsifier: A harmless process emits NUL plus non-UTF-8 octets; the exact byte sequence must round-trip through the serialized ClayVM unchanged.

counterhypotheses_and_required_falsifier.counterhypothesis: Capability denial can be bypassed by the new result accessor.
counterhypotheses_and_required_falsifier.falsifier: Without the required process capability, stdout access must fail closed independently of whether a receipt object exists.

counterhypotheses_and_required_falsifier.counterhypothesis: The new ABI widening perturbs legacy CLAYVM/1 or linux.process.spawn.v0 Int->Int behavior.
counterhypotheses_and_required_falsifier.falsifier: Existing serialized fixtures and process request-id regressions remain byte/behavior compatible unless an explicit versioned migration is introduced.

counterhypotheses_and_required_falsifier.counterhypothesis: call_id identity can be silently rebound across ABI evolution.
counterhypotheses_and_required_falsifier.falsifier: An incompatible registry rebind under an existing stable call_id must fail closed by ABI version/identity rather than reinterpret old bytecode.

make executable_ir_adapter import that registry instead of owning an independent HOSTCALL_SIGNATURES table
make ClayVM/ClayHost validate arguments and return values using that same registry
add linux.process.stdout.v0::(Int)->Bytes as the first real Bytes return contract backed by the existing completed HostProcessReceipt
add deterministic source/type/effect/signature mismatch, wrong return type, capability denial, unknown receipt, binary stdout and legacy compatibility regressions
run all execution as regression-only with new_unusual_experiment_count=0
when Vercel accepts the exact target head, run an actually-started exact-head Vercel Sandbox batch and, if carried into EntityOS, double-build and test the exact one-file artifact
